terms.name: Accessibility overlay
terms.definition: A third party script bolted onto a site with a promise of automatic compliance, usually a floating widget of font and contrast toggles that fixes nothing underneath.

terms.name: Agenda view
terms.definition: The same events as a chronological list grouped by day, so the next thing is at the top instead of somewhere inside a grid.

terms.name: Arc motion
terms.definition: Moving an element along a curved path rather than a straight line, so a change of position reads as natural rather than mechanical.

terms.name: Avatar group
terms.definition: Several avatars overlapped in a row to show a set of people compactly, with a plus n counter standing for the rest.

terms.name: Braille display
terms.definition: A refreshable braille row that renders the same accessibility tree as speech, with abbreviated role names authors can override.

terms.name: Canonical layout
terms.definition: One of a small set of proven multi pane arrangements a platform recommends, such as list detail, supporting pane and feed, instead of a new layout per screen.

terms.name: Chart aspect ratio
terms.definition: How wide a chart is for its height, which sets the slopes of its lines; banking to 45 degrees keeps rates of change readable.

terms.name: Coach mark
terms.definition: A temporary message anchored to a control that teaches what it does, often chained into a numbered sequence across a screen.

terms.name: Color theme
terms.definition: A complete named set of colour values a product can swap in whole, so light, dark, high contrast and per-tenant branding are the same mechanism.

terms.name: Concentric corner radius
terms.definition: Sizing a nested shape's corners so its curve shares a centre with the one outside it, the inner radius being the outer radius less the padding between them.

terms.name: Contrast ratio
terms.definition: A number from 1:1 to 21:1 describing how far apart two colours sit in relative luminance, used to decide whether text on a background is readable.

terms.name: Damping
terms.definition: The friction term in a spring that decides how quickly oscillation dies out, from a loose wobble to a critically damped move with no bounce at all.

terms.name: Density independent pixel
terms.definition: A virtual unit of length that stays the same physical size across screen densities, so one number can describe a layout on every device.

terms.name: Dithering
terms.definition: Adding fine noise to a gradient or image so the eye averages neighbouring pixels into the missing intermediate colours, hiding the bands.

terms.name: Drill-down navigation
terms.definition: Going deeper into a hierarchy one level at a time inside the same panel, each level replacing the last and offering a way back up.

terms.name: Elevation
terms.definition: How high a surface sits above the one behind it, expressed as a shadow, a tint, or both, and held to a few named steps so that height means something.

terms.name: Expandable row
terms.definition: A table row that opens to reveal a detail panel beneath it, keeping the row in place instead of navigating away.

terms.name: Feature spotlight
terms.definition: A one-time announcement pointing at something newly added, shown in place next to the feature and dismissed for good once acknowledged.

terms.name: Flat 2.0
terms.definition: Flat design with the depth cues put back in small doses: soft shadow, subtle gradient, and hover feedback that show what can actually be clicked.

terms.name: Focus plus context
terms.definition: A layout that keeps one region in full detail inside its own surroundings, shrinking or dimming the context instead of moving it into a second pane.

terms.name: Form
terms.definition: A grouping of controls a reader fills in and submits together, carrying the labels, validation and submit affordance for the whole set.

terms.name: Glyph
terms.definition: A single drawn shape in a font, which may be one character, a variant of one, or several characters fused together.

terms.name: Hamburger menu
terms.definition: A button of three stacked horizontal lines that opens a site's main navigation, usually in a panel over the page.

terms.name: Hit testing
terms.definition: Working out which element sits under a pointer, which decides who receives the event when shapes overlap or transparent areas are in the way.

terms.name: Icon
terms.definition: A small graphic symbol standing for an action, object or idea, read at a glance and rarely safe to ship without a label.

terms.name: Input group
terms.definition: A field welded to text, a button or a select at one or both ends, so the addon reads as part of the same control rather than as a neighbour.

terms.name: Jiggle mode
terms.definition: An editing state announced by making every rearrangeable item wobble in place, so the whole screen says it can be reordered.

terms.name: Label association
terms.definition: The programmatic link between a label and its field, made by for and id or by wrapping, which makes the label clickable and the field named.

terms.name: Letterboxing
terms.definition: Filling the mismatch between content shape and frame shape with bars: above and below for letterbox, at the sides for pillarbox.

terms.name: Live activity
terms.definition: A persistent, updating view of something in progress, shown in system places like a lock screen so a reader can follow it without opening the app.

terms.name: Marking pattern
terms.definition: A scanning shape where the eye holds one spot on the screen while content scrolls past underneath it, most common on phones.

terms.name: Metro
terms.definition: Microsoft's typography led design language of flat coloured tiles, large light headings, and motion used in place of chrome, shadow, and texture.

terms.name: Modular grid
terms.definition: A grid with both columns and rows, dividing the page into equal modules that content can span in either direction.

terms.name: Nagging
terms.definition: Interrupting a task again and again with the same request, so that agreeing becomes the cheapest way to be left alone.

terms.name: Non-breaking space
terms.definition: A space that renders normally but forbids a line break, gluing two words together so they never end up on separate lines.

terms.name: Operational transparency
terms.definition: Showing the work as it happens, the kitchen made visible, so a wait is understood rather than merely endured and the result is trusted more for having been watched.

terms.name: Oversized typography
terms.definition: Type set far past reading size so the words carry the layout, the headline doing the work a photograph would otherwise be hired for.

terms.name: Password strength meter
terms.definition: A gauge that scores a password while it is typed and names what would improve it, replacing a list of rules with continuous feedback.

terms.name: Pointer gestures
terms.definition: Path based or multi finger gestures such as pinch, swipe, and drag along a track, which need a single pointer equivalent to stay operable.

terms.name: Prime mark
terms.definition: The slanted tick used for feet, inches, minutes, and seconds, which is a different character from either a straight quote or a curly one.

terms.name: Pull to refresh
terms.definition: Dragging a list downward past its top edge to trigger a reload, with an indicator that appears in the space the drag opens up.

terms.name: Reaction picker
terms.definition: A small row of emoji that appears on hover or long press so a message can be answered without a reply.

terms.name: Resize text
terms.definition: Text must scale to at least 200 percent without loss of content or function, which rules out fixed pixel heights around wrapping copy.

terms.name: Roving tabindex
terms.definition: A focus technique where only one item in a group is in the tab order and arrow keys move that position, so Tab enters and leaves the whole group once.

terms.name: Scroll anchoring
terms.definition: Keeping the reader's position fixed when content loads or resizes above it, by adjusting scroll offset so the visible text does not jump.

terms.name: Seed color
terms.definition: The single input colour an algorithm expands into a whole scheme, so a palette becomes something derived from one decision rather than picked swatch by swatch.

terms.name: Shake to undo
terms.definition: Physically shaking a device to trigger undo or redo, an accelerometer gesture Apple defines system wide for reversing a recent edit.

terms.name: Slider
terms.definition: A control that sets a value by dragging a handle along a track, showing the whole range at once.

terms.name: Spacer
terms.definition: A deliberate empty element between regions: the gap between two panes that carries the drag handle when they resize, or the flexible filler that pushes toolbar items apart.

terms.name: Squash and stretch
terms.definition: Deforming an element along its direction of travel so it reads as having mass and flexibility, usually as a press squash or a launch stretch.

terms.name: Sticky footer
terms.definition: A footer held against the bottom of the viewport when the page is short, and pushed below the content when the page is long.

terms.name: Surface tint
terms.definition: A wash of the primary colour blended into a surface in proportion to its elevation, so height reads as a colour shift rather than only as a shadow.

terms.name: Table-based layout
terms.definition: Laying a page out in nested tables because the renderer has no box model worth trusting, which is how mail is still built and how the web was built before CSS.

terms.name: Throttle
terms.definition: Capping how often a continuous stream of input is acted on, so a response fires at a steady rate instead of on every event.

terms.name: Toolbar
terms.definition: A grouped row of controls acting on the current view, sharing one tab stop and moving focus between its items with arrow keys.

terms.name: Truncated axis
terms.definition: Starting a value axis above zero so differences look bigger than they are; honest for lines and dots, a lie for bars.

terms.name: Utility bar
terms.definition: A persistent bar docked to the bottom of an application holding small tools that open into panels without leaving the current page.

terms.name: Visual hierarchy
terms.definition: The ordering of elements by visual weight, size, contrast, position and spacing, so a reader learns what matters most without being told.

terms.name: Word spacing
terms.definition: The width of the gaps between words, which justification stretches and which, set too wide, opens rivers down a paragraph.
